question: Claim A4 was refuted on CAPACITY (ring size is recoverable from the distance pattern). This measures BEHAVIOUR: does the TRAINED head, on CLEAN geometry, actually close rings of the right size?

setup.head_z_table: all6 (width 18) -- REQUIRED; the default Pt-only table is width 13 and fails strict loading
setup.decision_rule: argmax over the 5 bond classes. NOTE the checkpoint's own bond_decision is 'threshold' at 0.5; this script uses argmax and says so.
setup.geometry: CLEAN tmQM coordinates -- in-distribution for a head trained on clean CSD structures

verdict: THE HEAD IS NOT THE RING DEFECT. On clean geometry the trained head's ring-size distribution is CLOSER to the real corpus than the truth bonds are: it UNDER-produces 3-rings and OVER-produces 5/6-rings relative to truth. The 89.81% three-membered rate in generated output therefore cannot be blamed on a head that, fed clean geometry, gets ring size right.
where_the_defect_must_live: Upstream, in the geometry the velocity field supplies. That is what ARCH-4 (make sampled geometry in-distribution) and ARCH-1 (the head never sees a noisy sample) address -- NOT the retrain slot for the bond head.
what_this_does_NOT_say: It does NOT say the head is fine. It predicts 305 rings against 657 in truth: it drops bonds. A correct ring-size DISTRIBUTION is not a correct ring-size COUNT.
It does NOT touch the macro-F1 deficit against OpenBabel (0.4784 vs 0.5051, metrics/by_metric/tmqm_bond_perception_3seed.json). That remains a real, separate honest-negative.
It rules out the specific hypothesis 'the head cannot do ring closure, so retrain it for that'. It does not rule out spending the slot on the macro-F1 deficit.
smoke_scale_caveat: 120 clouds, one checkpoint, one seed, CPU, no GPU. Directional, not a settled number.
